name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+22 partisan lean in a heavily Republican southwest Virginia district
Incumbent Morgan Griffith running with a large financial advantage ($974K vs $14K cash)
Prediction markets price Democratic chances at roughly 3%
No polling or expert ratings to suggest a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's R+22 lean, Griffith's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge leave challenger Joy Powers with minimal resources and no polling or outside support indicating a path. Markets price this near-certain Republican, so the forecast stays at a deep Republican margin.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or unexpected outside spending surge against Griffith would be the only realistic way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Morgan Griffith seeks another term in a southwest Virginia district that leans heavily Republican, about 22 points to the right of the country. He was renominated without difficulty and holds a commanding financial position, with roughly $974,000 on hand after raising nearly $1.8 million. Challenger Joy Powers has raised about $85,000 with under $14,000 available, and no outside groups have invested in the race.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, but prediction markets give Democrats only about a 3% chance. With the incumbent advantage, the district's lean, and the money gap all pointing the same direction, this race is rated Safe Republican.
